question: When replaying an argument that still stings, which way of thinking about it cools the anger rather than feeding it?
answer: Stepping back. People who recalled an anger-provoking memory as if watching themselves from a distance, and asked why it happened, felt less anger and had fewer angry thoughts than those who relived it through their own eyes. Same memory, same question; only the vantage point changed. A fly on the wall rarely shouts.
move: Look at a painful moment from outside before asking why it happened.
ask: Next time a conversation keeps replaying in my head, can I watch it as an outsider would?
reference: Kross, Ayduk & Mischel, When asking why does not hurt: Distinguishing rumination from reflective processing of negative emotions, Psychological Science, 2005
